newsitem.title: USA: Motorola Q3 net margin on sales 3.2 pct.
newsitem.headline: Motorola Q3 net margin on sales 3.2 pct.

text.p: Motorola Inc said net margin on sales was 3.2 percent in the third quarter, compared with 7.2 percent a year ago.
In the first nine months, net margin was 4.5 percent compared with 6.8 percent in the year-earlier period, said the telecommunications giant.

The company said earnings on the quarter were $206 million, compared with $496 million a year ago. Fully diluted earnings per common and common equivalent share were $0.34, down from $0.81 in the third quarter of 1995.
Shares in the company closed up one at 49-1/4.

Company president Christopher Galvin said the decline in earnings was due to "the recession in the semiconductor industry...competitive pressures and continuing price declines in cellular telephone, paging and modem businesses and the impact of weaker sales and order patterns on related component products such as rechargeable batteries."
"The earnings comparison is even less favorable due to a substantial net gain on the sale of certain assets in the third quarter of 1995," the company said.
Third-quarter sales in Motorola's general systems sector were off two percent to $2.6 billion, the company said.
Sales in the semiconductor products sector declined 19 percent to $1.8 billion compared with the year-ago quarter.
Third quarter sales in the messaging, information and media sector were up eight percent to $1 billion, while orders declined two percent, the company said.
"Operating profits were lower largely because of the substantial net gain recorded in the year-ago quarter from the sale of an investment," it said of the segment.
Sales in the land mobile products sector rose two percent to $929 million on the quarter.
Meanwhile, selling, general and administrative expenses decreased to 16 percent of sales in the third quarter from 17 percent a year ago, the company said.
Manufacturing and other costs of sales increased to 69 percent from 64 percent a year ago, due to more competitive pricing for semiconductors, the company said.
